5.1: `kubectl create configmap` accepts several sources in one command, so combine a literal flag with file-based flags.
`--from-literal=key=value` for the literal, `--from-file=./favorite` for the single file (key becomes the filename), and `--from-file=./tones/` with a directory makes one key per file.
5.2: Generate a Deployment skeleton and add the config injection in the container spec: one entry that picks a single key, and one that imports the whole ConfigMap.
Single key: `env[].valueFrom.configMapKeyRef` with `name` and `key`; all keys: `envFrom[].configMapRef.name`. Note `kubectl set env --from` uppercases keys, unlike `envFrom`.
5.3: Create the ConfigMap with `--dry-run=client -o yaml` for YAML output, then give the pod a volume sourced from that ConfigMap and mount it in the container.
Define it under `spec.volumes` with `configMap.name`, and mount it with `volumeMounts` using `mountPath: /etc/bike` and `readOnly: true`; each key appears as a file.
5.4: Create the Secret with `kubectl create secret generic` and a literal, then mount it as a volume in a Deployment (generate the skeleton and add the volume yourself).
A Secret volume uses `secret.secretName` (not `name` as for ConfigMaps); the key `entree` becomes the file `/food/entree` and `base64 -d` decodes the stored value.
5.5: Change the image with `kubectl set image`, record a reason on the Deployment, then use the `kubectl rollout` subcommands for history and undo.
`--record` is deprecated, so set the `kubernetes.io/change-cause` annotation with `kubectl annotate ... --overwrite`; `rollout undo` returns to the previous revision (or use `--to-revision`).
5.6: The update behaviour lives under the Deployment's `spec.strategy`; generate the Deployment with `--dry-run=client -o yaml` and add the settings.
Use `rollingUpdate.maxUnavailable: 0` and `maxSurge: 2`, plus `spec.minReadySeconds: 5` for the readiness delay; then trigger the update with `kubectl set image`.
5.7: Pause the rollout first so that several edits don't each trigger their own rollout, then resume once to roll everything out together.
Sequence is `kubectl rollout pause`, then `set image` and `set env`, then `kubectl rollout resume`; check that `rollout history` shows only one new revision.
5.8: Switch the strategy type of the existing Deployment to the one that kills all old pods first.
The type is `Recreate`, and the `rollingUpdate` block must be removed in the same change or the API rejects it; a JSON patch with `remove` and `replace` operations does both.
5.9: There is no generator for PV or PVC, so copy the manifests from the Kubernetes docs; the claim binds to the PV by matching storage class, access mode and size.

Both objects need `storageClassName: manual`; the PV uses `hostPath.path`, `capacity.storage` and `persistentVolumeReclaimPolicy: Retain`, and the PVC (namespaced, unlike the PV) requests 50Mi but will show the PV's full 100Mi once Bound.
5.10: Define the PVC once as a pod volume and mount that same volume into both containers at the same path.

Use `persistentVolumeClaim.claimName` under `spec.volumes`, and a `volumeMounts` entry with `mountPath: /var/log/nginx` in each container; the mount hides nginx's stdout symlink so a real `access.log` gets written.
5.11: Create a PVC first (the default StorageClass provisions it, so omit `storageClassName` and no PV is needed), then edit the Deployment to add a volume and a mount.

Plain kubectl has no `set volume`, so use `kubectl edit`; add a `volumeMounts` entry at `/newvol` and a `persistentVolumeClaim.claimName: reviewpvc` volume alongside the existing secret volume instead of replacing it.
5.12: Kustomize is built into kubectl; write a `kustomization.yaml` in the overlay that references the base via `resources` and uses its built-in transformer fields.

Fields: `namespace`, `namePrefix`, `images` (with `newTag`, quote "1.28" so it stays a string), `replicas` (name and count) and `configMapGenerator` with `literals`; preview with `kubectl kustomize` and apply with `-k`.
